tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_scm_xy COLD-SEASON single-column run, data/eqwefic/noahcold_scm, dumped by ctessum-claude/WRF branch earthsciml-instrumented-noahcold and replayed through the real64 (-fdefault-real-8) kernels/noah_driver at ESM_DT = 0.01 s. THE ASSERTED CLAIM is that the SUM of the two mounted tendencies reproduces WRF's own step: `dsh2o_dt_total` against (sh2o_out - sh2o_in)/dt, `dsmc_dt_total` against (smc_out - smc_in)/dt, and `dsice_dt` against the ice difference, all per layer. WRF forms none of these; it advances the water with SMFLX and then applies HRT's phase-change sink to what SMFLX has already moved, so this is a statement about the two components TOGETHER. THE REFERENCE STEP WAS CHOSEN BY MEASURING ITS V, not by assuming smaller is better (the rule is FORTRAN_BUGS N99 / PLAN section 6: a differenced reference HAS a cancellation floor, so its accuracy is a V in dt and the step is the minimum). Worst absolute residual over this document's assertions, at the three replay passes: 3.405e-11 at ESM_DT = 1e-6 s, 4.653e-15 at 0.01 s, 6.148e-15 at 60 s. The left branch is pure cancellation -- the liquid-water increment is only 1.6e-12 of sh2o at 1e-6 s, so the reference difference keeps about four digits, and the residual scales as 1/dt (a 10000x drop in dt raises it by 9000x). The right branch is the operator-splitting error plus WRF's interval clamp; on THIS column the clamp does not flip and 60 s costs only a factor of 1.3, but over the seventeen cold bare-ground columns the clamp decision flips at one layer of SIX of them at 60 s (0 -> 2, stopped at `free`), which turns the phase term into a finite-step artefact rather than a rate -- exactly the bind FORTRAN_BUGS N97 describes. 0.01 s is the minimum and it is four orders better than either end. TOLERANCES ARE THE REFERENCE'S FLOOR, NOT THE ASSEMBLY'S ACCURACY, and they are ABSOLUTE for a traced reason: the smallest layer tendency is 2.6e-12 per second while the top layer's is 3.8e-07, so a single relative bound would be meaningless. The floor is eps(sh2o)/dt = 2.2e-16 x 0.3 / 0.01 = 6.7e-15 per second; the measured worst residual over the three documents is 4.7e-15, i.e. AT that floor, and the published bound of 1e-14 is 2.1x it. The phase rate itself is asserted at abs 1e-18 and is exact, because it is referenced against the N97 publisher rather than any difference. `phase_active` and `supersaturation_active` are asserted at ZERO tolerance. THIS COLUMN: case A step 1, the only step in the whole cold reference set that takes the ACTIVE branch of the frozen-ground infiltration reduction (column ice 0.19 m against the 1e-2 m threshold), and one whose water supply is DEW rather than precipitation -- NOPAC adds the dew to the precipitation before the canopy split, so the column gains water with no rain at all. A different transport regime, on a different case, which is why it is a separate document rather than another assertion on the same one. It also carries the largest residual of the three, 4.7e-15, which is the number the 1e-14 bound is set from.
